lines: Si neſcis, oculi ſunt in amore duces.
Et voila pourquoy Iuuenal eſtime vne choſe prodigi-
euſe & trop eſtrange, qu'vn Aueugle ſoit amoureux. Et
Martial ſe mocque de Codrus, lequel priué de la veuë,
neantmoins depuis deuint extremement paſſiõné pour
l'amour d'vne femme.
Plus credit nemo, quam tota Codrus in vrbe,
Cùm ſit tam pauper, quomodo! cæcus amat. {c}
Et à laquelle ledit du Tilh auoit don
né pluſieurs priuées & particulieres en-
ſeignes. Meſmes des actes & propos qui
interuiennent le plus ſecrettement en-
tre mariez, & qu'autres ne peuuent bon
nemẽt ſçauoir, ou entẽdre: Iuſques à luy
enſeigner les lieux, temps, & heures des
actes ſecrets de mariage (plus aiſez beau
coup à comprendre, qu'honneſte à reci-
ter, ou eſcrire) & les propos qu'auant, a-
pres, & en l'acte, ils auroyent tenuz. S'e-
ſtoit auſsi perſuadée auec les autres, que
ledit du Tilh eſtoit certainement Mar-
tin Guerre ſon mari.
La femme de Q. Sertorius à Rome, & Ieanne fille
du comte Balduin de Flandres, furẽt vn peu mieux aui-
ſées: car quand celuy qui ſe diſoit fils de Q., Sertorius,
& de pluſieurs ſuiuy comme tel à Rome, vn iour ſe pre
ſenta à la femme de Sertorius cõme à ſa mere, luy don-
nãt des enſeignes fort familieres, & neãtmoins ſecrettes
& veritables: elle d'vne grande pertinacité, & vertueuſe
Properce an
liure ij. des ele
gies.

uncertain.text: Si neſcis, oculi ſunt in amore duces.
uncertain.note: Both reads set continues_prev true, assuming the hexameter of the Propertius couplet stood at the foot of p020. p020's final line is prose ('me dit Properce, ſont les guides, chefs & cõducteurs {b}.'), so this pentameter is quoted alone after a full stop; continues_prev set false. Paragraph block per §6

No marker b in the body of this page: the note with key b is printed at the top of the margin, beside body line 2. Its marker {b} is the last marker on p020 (final line 'me dit Properce, ſont les guides, chefs & cõducteurs {b}.'). Recorded here as a note without a body marker

Printed 'an' (sic): the sort after 'a' is joined at the top (arch) and open at the foot, unlike the italic u of 'liure' on the next line. A turned u for 'au liure ij.'; transcribed as printed. B read 'au' by sense; reconciled from the glyph

Same word as in note b, heavily inked; the top join is the likeliest reading, so 'an' (sic, turned u for 'au') as in note b. 'au' remains possible under the blot. Pointer: pages/full/p021.jpg x≈2150-2450, y≈1030-1090 (margin beside the Martial couplet)

uncertain.text: Cùm ſit tam pauper, quomodo! cæcus amat. {c}
uncertain.note: 'quomodo!' — the mark is a vertical stroke over a point, i.e. an exclamation, not the question mark the received text of Martial III.15 has. Transcribed as printed (sic); could conceivably be a damaged '?'.

uncertain.text: ſées: car quand celuy qui ſe diſoit fils de Q., Sertorius,
uncertain.note: After 'Q' the print sets a point and then a comma ('Q.,Sertorius,'), both clearly inked; normalized for spacing to 'Q., Sertorius,'. The comma looks like a compositor's slip; transcribed as printed. Line 1 of the same paragraph has plain 'Q. Sertorius'.

uncertain.text: nemẽt ſçauoir, ou entẽdre: Iuſques à luy
uncertain.note: The marks over the e of 'nemẽt' and 'entẽdre' are flat bars (tildes for the omitted n); B read them as acutes. Checked at 6x against the sloped acute of 'né' and 'priuées' in the same large fount; transcribed ẽ

uncertain.text: ſtoit auſsi perſuadée auec les autres, que
uncertain.note: 'auſsi' printed with long s + round s (both reads); as printed

uncertain.text: ſenta à la femme de Sertorius cõme à ſa mere, luy don-
uncertain.note: the line-end word-break sign after 'don' sits low and looks like a point; transcribed '-' per §1 (both reads)
'des ele' as printed (round s, then a word space); B wondered about 'de ſes ele' as on p006 note h; checked at 2.2x

at 2.2x (full page x≈2093-2677, y≈250-950) the two stems of the sort after 'a' are joined at the top by an arch and open at the foot, unlike the u of 'liure' on the next line (joined at the foot). Printed 'an', a turned u for 'au'; transcribed as printed, sic
at 3x (full page y≈950-1250) the sort is heavily inked; the top join is the likelier reading, the same form as in note b. Transcribed 'an', sic for 'au'; recorded as uncertain

both reads have the Propertius pentameter and the Martial couplet as paragraph blocks; confirmed per §6 (verse quotations are paragraphs, never headings); B's question about p010's practice is settled that way
agreed: marker {b} stands at the end of p020's last line ('cõducteurs {b}.'); the note is kept here with an uncertain entry
both reads assumed the couplet's hexameter ended p020; p020 (now final) ends with prose and the marker {b}, so the verse line starts a new quotation block
